rsm:PollutantRelease.rsm:RemarkText:
This calculation has derived from our most recent stack monitoring. 1. Calculate a volumetric flow inside the stack.
• This is done by multiplying the stack area (0.503m2) by the stack velocity (measured as 2.2m/s in September 2012)
0.503m2 * 2.2m/s = 1.106m3/s.
• Multiply by 3600 to convert from seconds into hours
1.106m3/s * 3600 = 3981.5m3/s at stack conditions.
2. Convert from stack conditions to reference conditions.
• This is done using the following equation
3981.5 * (ref temperature/measured stack temperature) * (Measure barometric pressure/ref pressure)
3981.5 * (273/308) * (1016/1013)
= 3539.5m3/hr. This is the volume of gas exiting the stack each hour.
3. Apply pollutant concentrations.
For each pollutant, multiply the emission concentration (in mg/m3) by 3539.5m3/hr.
e.g. naphthalene
130mg/m3 * 3539.5m3/hr = 460136mg/hr or 460.1g/hr or 0.460Kg/hr.
4. To calculate the annual emission, you would then be required to apply the number of hours that the scrubber was operational each year.
The scrubber ran for 1300hours, multiply by 1300
0.460Kg/hr * 1300hrs = 598Kg/year.
